To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

primary hepatocyte cultures are a useful model to study liver apoptosis and that the spontaneous apoptosis that develops in these cultures can be effectively inhibited by using appropriate culture conditions and by the addition of the apoptosis inhibitor Bcl-2.

the isolation and culture of hepatocytes is associated with a progressive increase in spontaneous apoptosis, which is accompanied by a concomitant increase in the expression of apoptosis biomarkers, and that these processes can be counteracted by the use of specific inhibitors of caspases and of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore.

(i) spontaneous apoptosis in primary hepatocyte culture can be prevented by the addition of a single supplement, i.e. 0.5% fetal calf serum (FCS); (ii) this effect can also be achieved by a combination of several supplements, i.e. insulin, dexamethasone and transferrin; (iii) the addition of 0.5-1% FCS to primary hepatocyte culture medium is a simple and reliable way to establish a long-term culture
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a reliable in vitro model for the study of apoptosis in primary human hepatocytes.

the identification of molecular mechanisms and signalling cascades involved in apoptosis induction in cultured primary hepatocytes and with their functional analysis in order to develop novel strategies to prevent or even treat apoptosis-related liver diseases.

the development of an experimental model system for the study of hepatocyte apoptosis, in which the spontaneous apoptosis occurring during isolation and cultivation of primary rat hepatocytes is counterbalanced by the addition of a specific anti-apoptotic agent, thereby allowing for a controlled induction of cell death.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of primary hepatocyte cultures in apoptosis research is feasible but requires a careful and critical evaluation of the experimental conditions.
the use of primary hepatocyte cultures in the field of apoptosis research has to be considered as a challenge.
the use of primary hepatocyte cultures is a very useful and valuable in vitro tool to study apoptosis in the liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

primary hepatocytes represent a valuable in vitro model for the study of apoptosis in general, but their application is restricted to short-term experiments, since their viability is limited to a maximum period of 7 days in culture.

the use of freshly isolated primary hepatocytes and their subsequent culture in the presence of serum and hormones, as well as the application of a variety of apoptosis-inducing agents are suitable tools to investigate the mechanisms underlying apoptosis in the liver.
apoptosis is a complex and highly regulated process that involves numerous molecular mechanisms and that is difficult to control and study in primary hepatocyte culture systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of primary hepatocyte cultures as an in vitro model system to study apoptosis in the liver has been and will remain an indispensable tool to advance our understanding of this complex and multifaceted process in health and disease.

primary hepatocytes can be cultured in a way that allows to study apoptosis and its underlying mechanisms, but the use of such cultures is not straightforward and requires careful consideration of a number of parameters.
the spontaneous induction of apoptosis is an intrinsic feature of primary hepatocyte cultures and that it is not possible to avoid it.
